reviews.title: Looks amazing, feels smooth, and sturdy
reviews.comment: Wish I could give it a 4.5, bumping it to a 5 as my only complaint was like others have mentioned, they do not label the pieces, only the screws and tools they provide have some labeling. This added a little time with assembly trying to ensure I had all of the pieces and verifying they matched the pictures since they weren't labeled. Once you get the pieces figured out, setup is actually pretty smooth. I was able to put this together solo in under an hour, again some time was spent figuring out the pieces and matching the pictures. I love the quality of the desk. I got the dark gray wood top, looks amazing and feels smooth. Planning on getting a large mouse pad as the top is split into 3. This hasn't been an issue using the mouse or anything, more of a comfort thing. The desk is very sturdy. It does wobble if you push it, but how often are you pushing or hitting your desk? Even raised up to the max height, I find it pretty sturdy. It will always wobble if you push it or put your weight into it (leaning on it), but I have personally had no issues with this. The other reason I can think of a wobble is if you have a large monitor. I have a 34" ultra-wide LG monitor on its stand and can see it move slightly if the desk moves, but this isn't really an issue as I'm typically not moving / shaking the desk. Finally, the motor on this thing is pretty quiet. It does not take too long to raise or lower it. I've seen some people rate the speed of it, but honestly how often are you raising and lowering the desk? Even if multiple times a day, the speed of it should not bother anyone. Hope that helps. I did take some time to finally buy the desk but glad I did! Worth it and for a great price (bought it on Black Friday).
reviews.author: Kevs_Ram06

reviews.title: Great work surface!
reviews.comment: *Husband review* Sent this to Seller on JAN-26-2024: "Sharp edges observed at leading edge of panel joining. Recommendations for safety & level: (1) Full-length joining channel at front & rear instead of four short channels. Middle panel least support - continuous passive/active downward load with resting hands on keyboard. (2) Thicker gauge screws for joining channels, need better grab per above. Otherwise.. very nice, very quiet desk, good price." Assembly was fairly easy. The only challenging aspect was setting the leg width AND drive rod simultaneously. Otherwise, you should have this together within 2 hours, max: 30-45 minutes for the frame, and the rest of the time putting the top together, placing it on the frame, and situating the desk. A cordless drill with a low speed/high torque and torque adjustment dial will make this even easier. You just need one #2 Phillips and one Allen wrench bits to get this done. No hammers or other tools needed. They made it very simple especially with having the motor already mounted. Great instructions, too. The height adjustment is surprisingly quiet and VERY smooth. You have four programmable pre-set buttons with a manual UP and DOWN button. The lowest possible setting with the provided casters is a typical sitting desk or dining table height. So, depending on how you prefer to elevate your hands/arms for typing and using your mouse, you might consider an undermount keyboard/mouse thingy. It feels like the desk can be manually increased/decreased by 1/8" increments -- you really should have no issue finding the right height for you. The frame has substantial enough weight to keep the top from feeling the slightest wobble. This was my biggest issue with my prior desk -- if I bumped it during a video call, it would wobble and look like I was having an earthquake. And the top is substantial enough to mount reasonably weighted items underneath. Not just baskets and tracks to hold cords and surge protectors, but PC mounts if, again, it's reasonable. Make sure your screw length won't penetrate the top surface. For what you set on top the desktop surface, follow the manufacturer's limits for combined weight. The frame box includes two of these cord holders. When mounted, they're out of sight - out of mind, so.. I don't have a use for them, yet! But I suppose they could hold headphones or a corded earbud/IEM. Maybe a few cords, dunno. I got the 32"Wx63"L unit. In hindsight, I might have gotten the longer desk (73" I think) because my old desk was sort of L-shaped, but I'm using less equipment now that I have a KVM switch for my 2-PC / 2-monitor set-up. So I should be good to go. UNRELATED TO THE DESK ITSELF BUT CRITICAL TO KEEP IN MIND.. Just be very clear AND CAREFUL when setting up your cable management, accessories, and living beings stored/visiting under ANY sit-stand desk: - My PC is on a standalone cart just inches from the floor, under my desk to mitigate sound/vibration issues. I had to ensure my HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-3.0 cables (A) were long enough at the DESK'S MAX HEIGHT position AND MONITOR PLACEMENT and (B) didn't cause a trip hazard since there's a walking path along the backside of my desk. Be mindful of the absolute max-height needed where all your connections occur. The last thing you want is to proudly sit at your new desk, press the button for max height, hark! the herald desk rises to glory, annnnnnd your monitors (assuming on stands and not mounted on arms) get ever so slightly tilted then violently pulled back only to plummet to their demise. - I have two large speakers and my PC tower/cart under my desk. I had to make sure at the lowest possible position, the motor would not crush/break or otherwise come in contact with the top of those items. Luckily, the speakers are ~3" away from the bottom of the motor, and the PC is set on the outside, between one of the legs and the wall. If you keep a filing cabinet or some other accessory under the desk, be aware of all elements under the desk's structural components during set-up. - Goes without saying.. Watch for small children and pets when raising and lowering the desk. When the desk achieves the lowest point, there are likely pinch points at the base of each leg.
reviews.author: Tracy or Andrew

reviews.title: Just buy it!!!
reviews.comment: I rarely leave reviews especially if the product works or is good, i just drop a 4 to 5 star rating and move on. But i wanted to take the time to write this review. This product exceeded my expectations. First of all, shipping was fast, got my desk in 2 business days. Price is very competative compared to the competition. Build quality is spectacular. This thing is heavy (recommend 2 people to asemble but I got away assembling it myself, just requires more time) but that means its built like a tank!! Very sturdy. Its very spacious and very ergonomic. It can literally adapt to your chair, even if your chair sucks, you can adjust the height of the desk to increase ergonomics. Assembly was relatively straight forward. Only feedback I can offer is labelling the different parts on the parts itself, makes it easier to follow along when reading the instruction manual as opposed to relying on the pictures as some parts come in multiples with slight variations and its really cumbersome trying to locate  the exact part the manual is refrencing. Otherwise, minor complaint. Still a 5/5. This thing is the only desk you'de ever need. Its a long term investment and i can see this lasting for years!!!
reviews.author: michael chukwu

reviews.title: Quiet motor, great design, but stability could be better
reviews.comment: The desk looks great and the overall quality feels solid. The motor is very quiet, much quieter than I expected, which makes adjusting the height feel smooth and effortless. Assembly was fast and the instructions were clear, so getting it set up was easy. The only downside is stability. When the desk is fully extended it feels wobbly and not as sturdy as I hoped. It is still functional, but you definitely notice movement. The desktop arrived with a few cosmetic marks due to shipping damage. This was disappointing, although it was not the manufacturer or seller’s fault. Their support team handled it quickly and professionally, so they earned five stars for service. Overall I am happy with the purchase. If the stability were better at full height, it would be a perfect five.
reviews.author: Max

reviews.title: Quality standing desk
reviews.comment: Very happy with this desk. It’s strong/stable even at the higher elevations I can still move around a lot with my mouse and not notice too much shaking. Stability is no issue for me personally with this desk! Very spacious and plenty of room for my equipment. I have three displays ontop of this desk along with 19in pen display and everything still holds up great. Setup was easy and instructions were clear enough for me to build this completely alone. I don’t recommend building it alone though.
